To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the introduction of an electron withdrawing group to the triphenylene mesogen results in a significant increase in the mesogenic range of the material and a more ordered mesogenic phase at lower temperature.

the introduction of a single electron withdrawing substituent on the triphenylene discotic mesogen leads to a significant enhancement in the mesogenicity of the material and that the optical properties of these materials are highly sensitive to the nature and position of the electron withdrawing substituent.
monofunctionalization and electron withdrawing groups have a dramatic effect on mesomorphic properties and fluorescence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, characterization and study of novel low symmetry discotic mesogens based on the triphenylene polyaromatic core, which exhibit interesting mesomorphic and photophysical properties.

the design and synthesis of new discotic mesogens that exhibit a broad range of mesophases, and the tailoring of the photophysical and electro-optical properties of these materials by the incorporation of functional groups on the triphenylene polyaromatic core.
the synthesis of new discotic liquid crystals and the correlation between their molecular structure and mesomorphic and photophysical properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new compounds are a new class of discotic liquid crystals which are unique in their mesomorphic and photophysical properties.
the mesomorphic and photophysical properties of triphenylene based liquid crystals are highly dependent on the number and type of substituents.
the mesomorphic and optical properties of these discotic liquid crystals are highly sensitive to small changes in molecular structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the introduction of a polar group to the triphenylene discotic mesogens results in a significant increase in the range of mesophases and in some cases the introduction of new mesophase types.
we have developed a general strategy for tailoring the mesomorphic and photophysical properties of triphenylene discotic liquid crystals.

the mesomorphic and photophysical properties of triphenylene discotic liquid crystals can be tailored by the introduction of a single functional group at the 1,8 position of the polyaromatic discotic core.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mesogenic properties and the optical properties can be tuned by varying the location and nature of substituent on the triphenylene discotic core.
the optical properties and mesomorphic properties of discotic liquid crystals can be controlled by the introduction of functional groups onto the triphenylene polyaromatic core.
the mesomorphic properties of triphenylene based liquid crystals can be significantly enhanced through the use of a single functional group.
